enzyme_name: nitrile-specifier protein (NSP) / non-enzymatic rearrangement of the glucosinolate aglycone
organism_context: Brassicaceae (Arabidopsis thaliana, Brassica rapa); indole glucosinolate (glucobrassicin) activation after tissue damage
rationale: The myrosinase-released indol-3-ylacetothiohydroxamate-O-sulfonate aglycone is intrinsically unstable and rearranges on its own; nitrile-specifier proteins (kelch-domain NSP1-5, Fe2+-dependent) only redirect its fate toward 3-indoleacetonitrile rather than acting as a classical single-substrate enzyme, so no catalysing enzyme can be assigned honestly.
direction_note: Aglycone decomposition to the nitrile is a one-way loss of sulfate and sulfur (ModelSEED status MI:O:-4/S:-2 flags exactly those missing atoms); nothing resynthesises a thiohydroximate-O-sulfonate from indole-3-acetonitrile, so ModelSEED's reverse call is chemically impossible.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous hydrolysis of indol-3-ylmethyl isothiocyanate
organism_context: Brassicaceae tissue and mammalian gut after glucobrassicin breakdown
rationale: Indolyl isothiocyanates are uniquely unstable among isothiocyanates and hydrolyse non-enzymatically to indole-3-carbinol plus thiocyanate; no protein catalyst is known or needed, so 'unknown' rather than a fabricated monofunctional assignment.
direction_note: A spontaneous hydrolysis releasing thiocyanate runs only one way; the ModelSEED reverse call would require indole-3-carbinol and thiocyanate to recondense into an isothiocyanate, which does not occur.

organism_context: Brassica tissue and the acidic mammalian stomach after glucobrassicin breakdown
rationale: 3,3'-Diindolylmethane is formed by acid-catalysed, non-enzymatic dimerisation of indole-3-carbinol with loss of formaldehyde and water; there is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: ModelSEED's status MI:C:-1/H:-4/O:-2 is precisely the missing formaldehyde + water; with those co-products dropped the thermodynamic estimate is meaningless, but the real condensation is one-way toward DIM.

organism_context: Plant family-1 UDP-glycosyltransferase; activity originally described in Silene/Melandrium and oat, and the same 2''-O-glucosylation of flavone C-glycosides is run by single-domain UGTs in rice, bamboo and Dendrobium
rationale: This is a plant GT1 (family-1) UDP-glycosyltransferase - a single GT-B domain with one glucosyl-transfer activity; I could not find a paper on the specific vitexin 2''-O-UGT protein, so the identity is inferred from the characterised 2''-O-glucosylating UGTs of the C-glycosylflavone pathway.
direction_note: Family-1 UGTs are effectively irreversible glucosyl donors in vivo; ModelSEED's reverse call would have a flavone glucoside regenerate UDP-glucose, which this enzyme class does not do at physiological UDP levels.

organism_context: Plant class I terpene synthases (e.g. Thymus, Origanum, Dipterocarpaceae); the alpha-terpinyl cation is the universal enzyme-bound intermediate of cyclic monoterpene formation from GPP
rationale: Monoterpene synthases have a single class I active site that ionises GPP, cyclises it to the alpha-terpinyl cation and then deprotonates it; multi-product behaviour at one site is not bifunctionality, and no separate enzyme handles the deprotonation half-step written here.
direction_note: This is a mechanistic sub-step of a composite cyclisation, not a standalone reaction - the alpha-terpinyl cation is never a free metabolite - but within the enzyme the only direction that occurs is cation -> alkene + H+, never protonation of alpha-terpinene.

organism_context: Plant class I terpene synthases (e.g. Solanum lycopersicum PHS1, Lavandula, conifers); same alpha-terpinyl cation branch point as rxn28182
rationale: A single class I terpene-synthase active site generates and then quenches the alpha-terpinyl cation; the alternative deprotonation regiochemistry that yields beta-phellandrene is a product-outcome difference, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Enzyme-internal half-step; the carbocation is quenched to the olefin inside the active site, so protonation of beta-phellandrene (ModelSEED's direction) is not a reaction any protein performs.

enzyme_name: nicotine-forming cascade: A622 (isoflavone-reductase-like NADPH reductase) + BBL (berberine-bridge-enzyme-like FAD oxidase), plus a UGT/glycoside-hydrolase pair in a cryptic activating glucosylation
organism_context: Nicotiana tabacum / N. benthamiana nicotine biosynthesis
rationale: Schwabe et al. (2026) reconstituted the nicotinate + N-methylpyrrolinium -> (S)-nicotine step as a four-enzyme stereoselective cascade (two glucose-processing enzymes plus the A622/BBL reductase-oxidase C-C bond-forming pair), so no single enzyme catalyses this ModelSEED entry.
direction_note: The real chemistry is an irreversible oxidative C-C coupling with decarboxylation (the lost CO2 shows up as ModelSEED status MI:C:-1/O:-2); nicotine is not converted back to nicotinate + N-methylpyrrolinium by this route, so ModelSEED's reverse call inverts a biosynthetic step.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - DAHP synthase + 3-dehydroquinate synthase + 3-dehydroquinate dehydratase (AroF/G/H, AroB, AroD) collapsed into one entry
organism_context: Shikimate pathway, universal in bacteria/plants/fungi; the PlantCyc entry carries no EC number
rationale: Erythrose-4-phosphate to 3-dehydroshikimate is the first three steps of the shikimate pathway; the missing atoms ModelSEED reports (status MI:C:3/O:-2/P:-1) are exactly the dropped PEP and two phosphates, so this is a lumped pathway segment, not an enzyme.
direction_note: The shikimate pathway runs E4P -> 3-dehydroshikimate and is driven by PEP consumption and two phosphate releases; ModelSEED's reverse call would make 3-dehydroshikimate a source of erythrose-4-phosphate, which no enzyme does.

organism_context: PlantCyc RXN-9043; no EC number, no KEGG cross-reference, no pathway assignment in the ModelSEED record
rationale: Searches on the substrate (3,4,6-trihydroxy-cis-cinnamate, MetaCyc CPD-8096) and on protocatechuate chemistry returned nothing that identifies a catalysing protein, and the equation is missing a two-carbon unit, so I cannot name an enzyme without fabricating one.
direction_note: ModelSEED status MI:C:-2/H:-2/O:-1 shows a whole C2 co-product (acetate/acetaldehyde-equivalent) is absent, so neither the ModelSEED nor the LLM direction rests on a complete equation.

enzyme_name: laccase (urushiol oxidase, multicopper oxidase) - with substantial non-enzymatic autoxidation
organism_context: Toxicodendron vernicifluum / T. radicans lacquer sap; laccase-initiated urushiol oxidation and radical coupling during lacquer hardening
rationale: Urushiol dimerisation during lacquer curing is initiated by sap laccase, a single multicopper-oxidase catalytic activity (a copper cluster is not a second activity), but much of the peroxide formation is uncatalysed autoxidation, so the enzyme attribution is weak.
direction_note: The equation is badly broken (ModelSEED status MI:C:42/H:56/O:6 - two dimers written against two monomers) and substitutes a fictitious H2 release for the real O2 oxidant; the true chemistry is one-way oxidation of urushiol, matching the LLM call.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana CSE (At1g52760), Populus tremula x alba CSE1/CSE2, Petunia, Larix; lignin/monolignol biosynthesis
rationale: CSE is a single-domain alpha/beta-hydrolase that hydrolyses caffeoyl shikimate to caffeate plus shikimate; the characterised CSE families in Arabidopsis, poplar and larch carry only this esterase activity.
direction_note: The shikimate co-product is missing entirely (ModelSEED status MI:C:-7/H:-8/O:-4); ester hydrolysis is effectively irreversible, and the reverse acylation is run by a different enzyme (HCT, using caffeoyl-CoA), so ModelSEED's reverse call attributes the wrong chemistry to CSE.

enzyme_name: umbelliferone 8-dimethylallyltransferase (U8DT), a membrane-bound UbiA-family aromatic prenyltransferase
organism_context: Apiaceae (Pastinaca sativa, Petroselinum crispum, Angelica keiskei, Ficus carica); osthenol is the committed precursor of angular furanocoumarins
rationale: Coumarin prenyltransferases are single-active-site UbiA-fold membrane proteins whose only activity is DMAPP-dependent C-prenylation; regiospecificity (C6 vs C8) is a substrate-positioning difference, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: Both DMAPP and the PPi leaving group are absent (ModelSEED status MI:C:5/H:8 is exactly the prenyl unit); prenyl transfer driven by PPi release is irreversible, so the reverse 'retro-prenylation' ModelSEED calls for has no enzyme.

enzyme_name: farnesyl diphosphate synthase (Erg20p); the BiGG ERG20_1 step is the DMAPP + IPP condensation (dimethylallyltranstransferase, EC 2.5.1.1)
organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (BiGG/iIN800 ERG20); homologous FPP synthases in plants, insects and humans
rationale: Erg20p carries two EC numbers (2.5.1.1 and 2.5.1.10) but both are the same head-to-tail 1'-4 prenyl condensation performed iteratively in one active site on a growing chain, not two distinct catalytic activities, so by the protocol's criterion it is monofunctional despite being loosely called 'bifunctional' in the literature.
direction_note: The product is mis-mapped to geranylgeranyl diphosphate (C20, cpd00289) when IPP + DMAPP can only give geranyl diphosphate (C10) - ModelSEED status MI:C:10/H:15 - but the real prenyl condensation is irreversible in the elongation direction because PPi is released and hydrolysed.

organism_context: Escherichia coli genome-scale models (iAF1260/iJO1366 lineage), where 5'-deoxyribose is a radical-SAM by-product with no consuming reaction
rationale: This is a modelling artefact added so 5'-deoxyribose can leave the network; there is no protein and therefore no functionality to classify.
direction_note: A demand reaction must run metabolite -> nothing; ModelSEED's '<' turns an empty left-hand side into a free source of 5'-deoxyribose, which would be a mass-creating loop in any model that uses it.

organism_context: Escherichia coli genome-scale models (iAF1260/iJO1366 lineage); aminoacetaldehyde is an ethanolamine-pathway dead end
rationale: Demand reaction, not an enzymatic step; no catalysing protein exists to classify.
direction_note: Same artefact as the other DM_ sinks: ModelSEED's reverse call makes the reaction a free source of aminoacetaldehyde rather than the intended outlet, despite the 'gold'-graded group-contribution number attached to it.

organism_context: Escherichia coli genome-scale models; 4-hydroxy-5-methyl-3(2H)-furanone arises from AI-2 / ribulose chemistry and has no consumer
rationale: Demand reaction, not an enzymatic step; nothing to classify.
direction_note: Direction must be out of the system; the ModelSEED reverse call inverts the sink into a source.

organism_context: Escherichia coli genome-scale models; oxamate is a dead-end product in these reconstructions
rationale: Demand reaction, not an enzymatic step; nothing to classify.
direction_note: Direction must be out of the system; the ModelSEED reverse call inverts the sink into a source.

enzyme_name: tetrathionate reductase TtrABC (TtrA catalytic molybdopterin subunit)
organism_context: Salmonella enterica sv. Typhimurium (SPI-2-adjacent ttrBCA operon), Shewanella sp. ANA-3, Vibrio parahaemolyticus; anaerobic tetrathionate respiration
rationale: TtrABC is a three-polypeptide membrane-bound respiratory complex (DMSO-reductase-family catalytic TtrA, Fe-S TtrB, quinol-oxidising anchor TtrC); per the protocol a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional, and TtrA itself carries only the tetrathionate-reducing activity.
direction_note: TtrABC is a terminal reductase: it is physiologically locked into tetrathionate + quinol -> 2 thiosulfate, and the reverse (quinone-dependent thiosulfate oxidation to tetrathionate) is run by entirely different enzymes (TsdA/DoxDA), so ModelSEED's reverse call assigns the wrong chemistry to this protein.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana plastidial ADT1-ADT6 (the source model is an A. thaliana reconstruction) and the periplasmic monofunctional cyclohexadienyl dehydratase PheC of Pseudomonas aeruginosa; the related E. coli PheA is a genuinely bifunctional chorismate mutase/prephenate dehydratase, but it acts on prephenate, not arogenate
rationale: The arogenate-utilising dehydratases are single-activity ACT-plus-PDT-domain proteins (the ACT domain is regulatory, not catalytic, so it does not count); the fused chorismate-mutase domain exists only in the prephenate-utilising PheA branch, which does not catalyse this reaction.
direction_note: Coupled decarboxylation and aromatisation make this step irreversible toward phenylalanine (the released water is missing from the equation, ModelSEED status MI:H:-1/O:-1); nothing carboxylates Phe back to arogenate.

organism_context: Escherichia coli / Enterobacteriaceae enterobacterial common antigen (ECA) biosynthesis, wec gene cluster
rationale: WecF is a single-activity inner-membrane glycosyltransferase that adds Fuc4NAc to lipid III; each wec-cluster step (WecB, WecC, WecD, WecE, WecF, WecG) is carried by its own monofunctional protein.
direction_note: The leaving nucleotide is mis-mapped to cpd00056 (thiamine pyrophosphate) instead of dTDP - ModelSEED status MI:...S:1 is thiamine's spurious sulfur - so the thermodynamics behind the reverse call are computed on the wrong molecule; the real sugar-nucleotide transfer runs forward.

enzyme_name: allene oxide synthase (AOS; hydroperoxide dehydratase, CYP74A, EC 4.2.1.92)
organism_context: Arabidopsis AOS (At5g42650) and plant orthologues in the jasmonate branch of the oxylipin pathway; note that the wider CYP74 clan does contain genuinely bifunctional epoxyalcohol synthase/AOS members (e.g. lancelet CYP74-clan enzyme), but the canonical plant CYP74A is single-activity
rationale: Plant CYP74A is a single catalytically self-sufficient P450 (no O2 or reductase needed) whose only activity is dehydration of 13-HPOT to the 12,13-allene oxide; the reported bifunctional EAS/AOS enzymes are different CYP74 clan members.
direction_note: The released water is missing (ModelSEED status MI:O:-1), and the allene oxide product is so unstable (half-life of seconds in water, handed straight to allene oxide cyclase) that the reaction cannot run backwards - ModelSEED's reverse call is physically impossible.

enzyme_name: trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline dehydrogenase (HypDH/LhpD; PRODH2 in mammals), FAD-dependent
organism_context: Sinorhizobium meliloti, Pseudomonas, and human PRODH2; the closely related proline counterpart PutA is a genuinely bifunctional PRODH/P5C-dehydrogenase in E. coli, but hydroxyproline dehydrogenases are separate single-activity flavoenzymes
rationale: HypDH is a standalone FAD-binding (beta/alpha)8 proline-dehydrogenase-fold protein with only the hydroxyproline-oxidising activity; the downstream P5C/dehydrogenase step in hydroxyproline catabolism is encoded by a separate gene, unlike the fused PutA of proline catabolism.
direction_note: Writing free FAD/FADH2 hides what actually makes this reaction unidirectional - the enzyme-bound flavin is re-oxidised by the membrane quinone pool - so the thermodynamic estimate (near zero, eQ 16.7 kJ/mol) has no bearing on the real direction, which is oxidation of hydroxyproline.

organism_context: Fused PRAI-IGPS on one chain in Escherichia coli and other Enterobacteriaceae (trpC); in S. cerevisiae TRP3 instead fuses IGPS to the anthranilate synthase glutamine amidotransferase. The two activities are on separate monofunctional proteins in plants (including Arabidopsis, the organism of the source model) and in archaea such as Sulfolobus.
rationale: E. coli trpC encodes a single polypeptide carrying both the PRAI isomerase and the IGPS ring-closure activities on separate (beta/alpha)8 barrel domains; per the protocol, lineage-restricted fusion still counts as bifunctional.
direction_note: Both fused domains run in the tryptophan-biosynthetic direction, so bifunctionality does not explain the conflict here - the irreversible decarboxylation/ring closure does (and the released water is missing from the equation, ModelSEED status MI:H:-1/O:-1).

organism_context: Bacteria, fungi and plants; in Bacillus subtilis the 60-mer RibH capsid encloses the riboflavin synthase trimer to form the alpha3beta60 'heavy riboflavin synthase' - a multi-subunit complex of two separate gene products, not a fused bifunctional chain
rationale: Lumazine synthase carries one condensation activity; the riboflavin synthase activity that completes the pathway sits on a different polypeptide (RibE/RibC) that merely co-assembles with it, which the protocol excludes from bifunctionality.
direction_note: The two water molecules the real condensation releases have been abstracted into a spurious O2 + 4 H+ (ModelSEED status is charge-imbalanced CI:3 with mass nominally OK), which fabricates an oxidation and is what drags the eQuilibrator estimate to a reverse call; the enzyme only ever runs the condensation, whose product is immediately consumed by riboflavin synthase.

enzyme_name: NAD(P)H-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase / (E)-2-hexenal reductase of the green-leaf-volatile branch of the oxylipin pathway
organism_context: Plant green-leaf-volatile formation after wounding (Arabidopsis, maize, tomato); downstream of lipoxygenase and hydroperoxide lyase
rationale: The hexenal/hexenol interconversion is a single zinc- or SDR-type alcohol dehydrogenase activity; the plant ADHs assigned to this step carry no second catalytic function.
direction_note: The NAD(P)+/NAD(P)H couple has been dropped entirely, leaving a bare '2 H+', so the enzyme has no intrinsic direction here - alcohol dehydrogenases are freely reversible and the in-planta flux (hexenal -> hexenol after wounding, which is the LLM's side) is set by the pyridine-nucleotide pool, not by the protein.
